language.script_notes: English and Swahili both appear on official signage, a legacy of British colonial rule; road signage style closely resembles the UK's given that history.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Black-and-white striped bollards found near intersections in Nairobi and Mombasa; largely absent outside large towns/cities.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel guardrail on major roads; often minimal on rural roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: White outside/yellow inside center lines, often dashed.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in city centers; minimal shoulder definition on rural roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Total, OiLibya, VivoEnergy and KenolKobil are common fuel-station brands. Safaricom (Kenya's dominant telecom brand, green-and-white) signage is extremely visible nationwide — a strong Kenya-specific tell.

architecture.roof_style: Simple pitched roofs, very commonly rusted corrugated metal — a strong visible national tell.
architecture.roof_material: Rusty corrugated metal roofing is disproportionately common and visible from a distance nationwide.
architecture.wall_construction: Concrete-block and painted-brick construction common in towns; ornate carved wooden doors on Swahili coastal architecture near Mombasa.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Often brightly painted shopfronts advertising Safaricom/mobile-money and consumer brands; muted concrete-block tones elsewhere.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Swahili coastal architecture with ornate carved doors near Mombasa; Nairobi's modern skyline set directly against open savanna on its eastern edge (Nairobi National Park); simple rural shops and roadside stalls.

nature.vegetation: Flat-topped acacia trees are a defining East African savanna tell; open grassland dotted with acacia across the highlands and Athi Plains; denser vegetation near Mount Kenya and the coast.
nature.terrain: The Great Rift Valley runs north-south, dividing highland plateau from lower plains; Mount Kenya (Africa's second-highest peak) rises as a glaciated volcanic massif; a stretch of Indian Ocean coastline in the southeast.
nature.climate_signature: Warm and dry across much of the savanna interior; cooler and more temperate in the highlands around Nairobi and the Rift Valley; humid tropical along the coast.

vehicles.plate_color: A long white plate on the front and a short, stubby yellow plate on the back is a distinctive and reliable Kenya-specific format.
vehicles.plate_format: Newer format: three letters, three digits, then a final letter (e.g. 'KXX 123A').
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Matatus (brightly decorated shared minibus taxis) are a strong East Africa tell; the Google Street View car in Kenya is notable for a visible black snorkel on the front, shared with only a few other countries (Guatemala, Senegal).

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of official Google coverage and Trekker imagery outside major cities.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Denser around Nairobi and Mombasa; sparser in rural/interior areas.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared East African Community membership, similar matatu/van culture, similar Swahili/English signage conventions in parts
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Uganda is landlocked with no coastline, unlike Kenya's Indian Ocean coast; Uganda's shared-taxi van livery patterns differ subtly from Kenya's, and Uganda lacks Kenya's Safaricom-branded signage density (MTN is more dominant there).

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Swahili-English bilingual signage, similar savanna vegetation and East African coastal architecture, both have Indian Ocean coastlines
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Kenya's Google car has a distinctive visible snorkel on the front, a detail not present the same way in Tanzania's coverage; Safaricom's green-and-white branding dominates Kenya specifically, while Tanzania's mobile brands differ.
